title: How U-Boot finds and starts Linux

steps.title: A chain of environment variables
steps.body:
U-Boot's boot is not hard-coded: `bootcmd` runs `bsp_bootcmd`, which runs a series of variables. The left column is the flow; the right column shows this board's real boot log for each step.

Every step can be printed, changed or overridden from `/boot/uEnv.txt`.

steps.anchor: Hit any key to stop autoboot: 1 s
steps.title: A one-second window to interrupt
steps.body: `bootdelay=1` gives you one second to press a key and get the `u-boot=>` prompt before `bootcmd` runs. You need the serial console connected to use it.

steps.title: Pick the device it booted from
steps.body: `mmcdev` is the MMC device number U-Boot booted from: 1 for the SD card, 2 for the eMMC. The log shows `mmc1 is current device`, meaning the SD card.

steps.title: Two optional override files
steps.body:
If `/boot/boot.scr` exists, U-Boot sources it and the script decides everything. Otherwise it imports `/boot/uEnv.txt` to override variables and continues.

The log lines `Failed to load` for both are normal, since neither file exists by default.

steps.title: Load and unpack the kernel
steps.body:
`loadimage` reads `/boot/Image.gz` from partition 1 into `${img_addr}` and unzips it to `${loadaddr}`. The log shows 15,647,614 bytes read and an uncompressed size of 35,887,616.

If that fails, U-Boot falls back to netboot: DHCP, then TFTP.

steps.title: Size the CMA pool from RAM
steps.body:
CMA (contiguous memory allocator) is memory the kernel reserves for devices such as the GPU and camera. The size depends on RAM: 64M up to 512 MiB, 320M to 1 GiB, 384M to 2 GiB, else 704M.

This board has 4 GiB, so it gets `cma=704M`.

steps.title: Build the kernel command line
steps.body: These variables assemble `bootargs`, the text passed to Linux: `console=ttymxc1,115200 root=/dev/mmcblk1p1 rootwait rw cma=704M`. Wrong `root=` and the kernel cannot mount its root filesystem and stops.

steps.title: Derive the device-tree name
steps.body:
U-Boot builds the DTB file name from the module (read from EEPROM), its revision and the carrier board. Here it gives `imx8mp-var-som-1.x-symphony.dtb`.

A wrong name means the kernel gets no or the wrong hardware description.

steps.title: Jump into the kernel
steps.body: `loadfdt` reads the DTB and `booti` starts the kernel, passing the DTB address. The log ends in `Starting kernel ...` and U-Boot is gone from memory.
